newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs stay soft, Med Aframaxes fall.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs stay soft, Med Aframaxes fall.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates remained soft on Monday, continuing last week's trend, brokers said.

Rates to most destinations except Japan remained below the W50 mark, with the 265,000 tonne Astro Gamma fixed at W45 Mideast/Red Sea for Exxon, loading May 5 and the Diamond Grace fetching W47.5 Mideast/Singapore for SPC.
Even modern vessels to South Korea fetched below W50, with the 1994-built Berge Stadt said fixed at W49 for Yukong.
But brokers said modern ships to Japan were holding up reasonably well at W55/57.5.
The West Africa market, which was active last week, was quiet on Monday, although brokers said they saw no reason to lower the rate for West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs from W67.5.
However, despite the busy market last week, this was still lower than the March average of W72.06, according to Reuters Tanker Industry Index .

In the Mediterranean, Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) dipped to around W110 from W125 on a lack of enquiry. "There are few cargoes around and a number of vessels are ballasting back to the Med from the Continent," one broker said. Med Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) were flat at about W95 while inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes edged down to W97.5 from W100.
Fuel oil 25,000 tonne cargoes were fixed at W185 in quiet trade in both the north and the Med, brokers said.

In the Western Hemisphere, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes were little changed at W225 while 50,000 tonne fuel oil vessels fetched about W162.5, continuing the softness in that sector seen on Friday, brokers said.
